claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I do. I have a child, Alex, who is 9 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions:

Are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does Alex live with you, or do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards the cost of supporting Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with money for his expenses - things like clothes, school costs, that sort of thing. I send money regularly to help support him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if you meet the responsibility test, I need to understand the amount you're contributing.

Do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child) towards Alex's upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute more than that. I send £30 a week to help with Alex's costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Now I need to ask about Alex's living arrangements:

Where does Alex live, and who does he live with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mother. They have their own place together.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to ask an important question about the living arrangements:

Is Alex's mother currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she isn't claiming Child Benefit for him. Nobody else is getting it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

Is Alex in full-time non-advanced education or approved training? And does he normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is only 9, so he's just in primary school. And actually, no - we don't live in the UK. We're abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. This is an important detail. 

Can you tell me which country you and Alex are currently living in? And are you or Alex's mother working for a UK employer, the UK government, or receiving certain UK benefits while abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad - not in the UK. Alex lives with his mother, and she's also not in the UK. We're not working for UK employers or the government, and we're not receiving UK benefits while we're overseas.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have enough details now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me, I need to give you my assessment:

**Unfortunately, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

The main reason is the residency requirement. To claim Child Benefit, either you or the child must normally live in the UK. Since you've confirmed that:
- You are living abroad (not in the UK)
- Alex is living abroad with his mother (not in the UK)
- Neither you nor Alex's mother are working for a UK employer or government
- You're not receiving UK benefits while overseas

This means the residency condition is not met, which is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

While you do meet the responsibility test by contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit rate), and no one else is claiming for him, the residency requirement cannot be satisfied in your current circumstances.

If your or Alex's circumstances change and either of you return to live in the UK, you may become eligible at that point.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. So it's really about living in the UK then - even though I'm supporting him financially, because we're both abroad, I can't claim it. Thank you for explaining that to me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're absolutely right - you've understood it correctly. The UK residency requirement is essential for Child Benefit eligibility, and even though you're doing the right thing by supporting Alex financially, being abroad means you don't meet that key condition.

You're welcome, and I'm sorry the outcome isn't what you were hoping for. If circumstances change in the future and you or Alex return to the UK, it would be worth looking into this again.

Let me now formally record this assessment.
